correctness.rationale: PASS: Signals decompose in the jump basis h^(k) modulo constants; the variation norm is exactly the maximum l1-column sum of D S_n^r D^{-1}. Direct counting of all n insertions yields a nonnegative upper-bidiagonal gradient matrix B, zero first column and common surviving column total q=(n-1)/n. After division by q it is a substochastic downward-stay Markov kernel with monotone coupling; hence the last jump is a global maximizer at every r. From the largest state the independent geometric waits to descend have success probabilities 1/(n-1),..., (n-2)/(n-1), whose sum equals T_{n-1}-1, so survival after r steps is exactly P(T_{n-1}>r) (including r=0 and n=2). Inclusion-exclusion and the first all-distinct coupon completion give the exact formula and first deficit; factorial moments of unseen coupons yield Poisson(e^-t) and the critical profile. Inverse-permutation enumeration gives the transpose norm 0 for n=2,1 for n=3 and 2-2/n for n>=4. Independently constructed rational insertion matrices and step seminorms for n=2..7 and powers 0..11 agree; finite runs do not prove the all-n claim.

value.rationale: PASS: The natural operator describes repeated averaging of an ordered numerical signal under a standard card shuffle. Its exact all-time contraction strength has a coupon-collector stopping-time interpretation, a surprising delayed strict-deficit horizon, a nontrivial Gumbel-shaped critical-window norm, and an adjoint contraction/amplification contrast. Those are useful stability invariants, not merely the known mixing time rephrased.
